text:
Sam: Quick design check — we have a responsive chart where the legend collapses into a single "compact" pill at small widths (see figma link). Behavior: pill shows total series count and toggles a flyout. Question: is hiding series names + relying on flyout ok for keyboard users / screen readers? Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/console-charts

Priya: I think hiding the labels by default is fine visually, but accessibility-wise we must ensure keyboard focus lands on the pill and the state is announced. Suggest making the pill a real <button aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="legend-list" aria-label="Show legend (3 series)"> with a visually hidden label like "Show legend (3 series)". Also ensure the flyout is focus-trapped while open.

Miguel: @Priya +1 on the button. Implementation note: we already have a Popover component that handles focus trap, but it doesn't set an aria-live. We could add aria-live on the popover content for dynamic announcements.

Ava: UX nit: When the legend collapses, the color swatches still convey mapping but people expect to see the name on hover. Can we include short tooltips for each swatch in the flyout? Also consider a compact inline list option instead of an overlay for dashboards where flyouts are clipped.

Jordan: From PM: main goals are discoverability and low clutter. If keyboard users can open the pill with Enter/Space and then arrow between items, that meets our needs. Metrics: want to avoid extra clicks for power users. Maybe default to expanded on wider breakpoints and collapsed only when space < 520px.

Priya: Accessibility details:
- Use: <button aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="legend-list" aria-label="Show legend, 3 series">Legend • 3</button>
- When opened: move focus into the list root <ul id="legend-list" role="listbox"> and support arrow keys + space to toggle series visibility.
- Add an aria-live="polite" region for state changes like "Series X hidden".
- For screenreaders, announce the collapsed status: "Legend collapsed, press Enter to open".

Miguel: Implementation trade-offs:
- Adding listbox + roving tabindex is extra JS but we already have utilities for roving focus.
- aria-live updates may be noisy on rapid toggles; debounce to 250ms and coalesce messages: e.g., "2 series visible, 1 hidden".
- For hover tooltips we can use title attr fallback, but prefer a11y-specific tooltip component for keyboard users.

Ava: Visual suggestions:
- Show small caret on the pill to indicate expandable control.
- When flyout opens, include a compact "search" at top for large dashboards (helpful when >10 series).
- Keep smoothing toggle separate from legend; smoothing affects curve shapes but not legend state. Default smoothing = off in perf dashboards (per analytics).

Jordan: Decision proposal:
1) Make pill a proper button with aria-expanded + aria-controls.
2) Use popover component with focus trap and roving focus for items.
3) Add aria-live for state changes with 250ms debounce.
4) For tiny viewports where popover would clip, fall back to a full-width inline drawer.
5) Add tooltip labels for swatches and optional search in flyout for >6 series.
Can design team sign off?

Sam: This is great — @Priya can you draft the exact ARIA strings / microcopy? @Miguel can you prototype with our Popover and roving focus? @Ava can you update figma with the caret + drawer fallback? I can add a small QA checklist for accessibility tests.

Priya: I'll post the microcopy in this thread tomorrow. Quick sample: "Legend collapsed. Press Enter to open legend. Use arrow keys to navigate series. Press Space to toggle visibility."

Miguel: I'll spike a prototype tonight, will post a short screen recording. :thumbsup:
